name: Tomasz — 40 thermic hours, flying hard, excellent in every other respect
summary: Flies weekly, 150 hours total, advanced ground handling, reliable launches across a range of sites, practises asymmetrics and spirals regularly, plans and reads days well, phase-aware hands, 10km cross-countries becoming normal. Around 40 hours of thermic time, because he came to thermalling late after two seasons of coastal flying.
why_this_persona: The pilot the whole 'fuzzy evidence governs method, asymmetric risk governs level' decision is about. He is short of the published thermic-hours range — which starts at 75 on its most generous reading — and strong at everything else. Two things have to happen and only two: he must NOT be capped by a gate (he is flying hard, so the combination clause protects him), and he must be held at Nearly ready by the thermic-hours Ready-blocker. If a reviewer ever makes the thermic gate unconditional at the 25-50 band, this is the persona whose result wrongly flips to Not yet.

notes: Computed skills 82.4, psychological 88.8, total 85.4, no bonus. His total and both category floors clear the Ready thresholds comfortably, so the ONLY thing holding him at Nearly ready is the thermic-hours Ready-blocker — which makes him the cleanest test of it in the set.

NO GATE fires, and that is the load-bearing assertion. 'thermic_hours_low_and_thin_currency' matches his thermic band (25_50) but requires thin currency alongside it: he is at 50-80 hours in the last 12 months and flying weekly, so the gate correctly leaves him alone. A scorer that makes that gate single-answer caps a pilot who is doing exactly the right thing about the gap.

The message he sees names the 75-to-100-plus RANGE and says out loud that one retailer's own two articles disagree. Per config/scoring/high-b-to-low-c.json rule_messages.display.tone_rule, no message at this step may present that range as a single number — this is the message most likely to drift, so it is worth reading in full against knowledge/disagreements.md points 2 and 6.

'performance_chasing_reframe' must NOT fire. He answers 'I want more glide and speed' — which the scoring config marks down one notch to 0.7 but never gates on — AND he can name the flights his wing cost him. The suggestion requires both the motive and the ABSENCE of limiting evidence, so a pilot who wants performance and has earned the claim never sees it. knowledge/disagreements.md point 9 requires exactly that split.

'xc_experience_build' fires on 'around 10km is normal for me now', which is real cross-country flying and scores 0.7. It is a suggestion, not a shortfall: the body states Joy Paragliding's counter-argument that kilometres say little about wing choice, and resolves the tension rather than picking a side.

'reading_the_day_drill' must NOT fire — he answers 'usually read it' (0.8). This is worth asserting because this step tightens the reading_the_day bar one notch relative to mid-B to high-B, and the tightening must bite only at 'right about half the time', not above it.

TONE CHECK: by any general measure of flying ability he is stronger than persona 09, who scores lower, and he is short of one number at a boundary the industry itself argues about. The result has to land as information, not as a reprimand, and the rule message is written for exactly this pilot.
